findingsCorrected.finding: Existing discovery guidance did not establish that every selected case produced measurements.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A successful JMH command and nonempty JSON could be accepted as complete evidence while failed cases were omitted.
findingsCorrected.fix: Reconcile selected cases, completed results and failure logs before interpreting scores; route detailed strict/partial-run policy to the reference.

findingsCorrected.finding: Result auditing lacked a concrete distinction between selection exclusions and failures under JMH 1.37's default continue-on-error behavior.
findingsCorrected.consequence: Surviving results can change a comparison's input population; an intentionally narrowed run could also be incorrectly rejected as incomplete.
findingsCorrected.fix: Trace the actual artifact/launcher/options, inspect discovery and effective run metadata, reconcile configuration/fork observations, verify strict failure behavior with a controlled probe, and preserve intentional partial sweeps.

validation.executionPurpose: The three tiny SingleShot runs resolve a material CLI failure/coverage claim. Durations are not performance evidence and no timing comparison was made.
expectedNegativeControls: Deliberate benchmark exception under default policy demonstrates false-success if only process exit/result presence is checked.
Same error under -foe true confirms strict propagation.
Intentional subset selection confirms that one result is complete when one case was selected.
validation.warnings: JMH 1.37 prints terminally deprecated sun.misc.Unsafe warnings on JDK 25. Kept in logs; not suppressed. Checks completed for their stated purpose.
validation.structuredWalkthroughs: Reviewed the two saved actor cases against the separately defined criteria: incomplete selected population versus complete explicit subset. No independent actor output.

retainedArtifacts.replay: VALIDATION.md records the exact compile/discovery commands; run-controls.ps1 records all executed launches and assertions. All generated harnesses, results, failure logs and source contracts are retained.

reproducibleCases.actorInput: Audit whether smoke-run.md correctly reports measurement coverage of the selected parameter population. Inspect the source, launcher command, full run log and JSON result; update the report only. Preserve this intentionally short diagnostic lifecycle and the Java/JMH versions. No new benchmark run is needed, and these control scores must not become a performance claim.

sharedFixtures.README.md: This is a diagnostic harness smoke run, compiled with --release 17 and JMH 1.37 and executed on Temurin 25.0.3. The short single-shot lifecycle checks selection/failure reporting, not timing quality. The report should cover the configured input population, including failed configurations; continuing through failures is intentional for this diagnostic sweep.

commonCriteria: Inspect actual command and its parameter override, source @Param values, full log and result records; exit 0 and nonempty JSON alone are insufficient.
Keep the diagnostic purpose, existing versions and deliberately short lifecycle.
Do not turn recorded durations into a speedup or production claim.
Respect report-only scope and do not require another benchmark campaign.

pass: Identify both good and broken were selected, but only good produced a result and broken threw the deliberate exception.
Correct smoke-run.md to state incomplete measured coverage of the selected population while retaining the failed case and its evidence.

Explain JMH 1.37's default continue-on-error behavior; strict -foe true can be mentioned for a different strict-run requirement, but the intentional diagnostic sweep does not require changing its policy.
fail: Retain the complete-measurement claim because exit code is 0.
Treat the missing broken row as a zero cost or exclude it silently.
Force fail-fast despite the explicit diagnostic-sweep requirement.
Infer valid comparative timing from one single-shot measurement.

pass: Read the -p input=good override and recognize that the selected population contains one case.
Keep the complete-coverage statement bounded to good; broken was not selected, and its absence is not a hidden execution failure.
Do not demand restoring every source @Param value, rerunning everything or changing the failure policy without a changed requirement.
fail: Treat B as the same incomplete selected population as A by reading only the annotation.
Claim broken succeeded or all source-declared cases were measured.
Interpret the intentionally short run as statistically valid performance evidence.

evaluatorCriteriaSeparated.isolation: Actor and criteria files are separated for materialization, not a technical access boundary.

reproducibleCases.decisiveConstraint: Only selected input population changes: A uses @Param's good and broken; B's explicit -p override selects only good. Logs/results are the corresponding observed outputs.
reproducibleCases.prerequisites: Fresh file workspace per case, read/edit access to the materialized actor fixtures and selected skill snapshot. No new benchmark run, dependency installation or production access required.
reproducibleCases.isolation: Keep criteria, other case and full handoff outside actor access. Saved separation is procedural; coordinator must enforce or audit it.
